## D4-03 · A partial index that doesn't match the query

> **GENERATED · written for this system (reinforces a concept from the source)**  
> Source: [lecture5 L917-924](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“because my WHERE clause included 2023”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C4.5 | ★★★ |  | `movies` | change the database |

Searching this year's titles should use a partial index. The query is `SELECT "title" FROM "movies" WHERE "year" = 2023;`.
The index below isn't used. Write one that is (name it `recents`).

```sql
CREATE INDEX "recents" ON "movies" ("title") WHERE "year" = 2022;
```

## D4-04 · A transfer that created money

> **SOURCE · demonstrated in the lecture**  
> Source: [lecture5 L1285-1296](../sources/lecture5.txt) *“So I need to undo this but I don't have a transaction here.”*

| Topic / concepts | Difficulty | Skills | Dataset | Task type |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C4.7 | ★★★ |  | `bank` | change the database |

Alice ($0) "pays" Bob $10. The debit fails its CHECK, but Bob keeps the $10, so the bank now holds $70 instead of $60.
Rewrite it so a failure leaves both balances untouched. (Statements keep running after an error here.)

<details><summary>Setup</summary>

```sql
UPDATE "accounts" SET "balance" = 0 WHERE "id" = 1;
UPDATE "accounts" SET "balance" = 30 WHERE "id" = 2;
```
</details>

```sql
UPDATE "accounts" SET "balance" = "balance" + 10 WHERE "id" = 2;
UPDATE "accounts" SET "balance" = "balance" - 10 WHERE "id" = 1;
```

<details><summary>Bug type</summary>

`transaction`
</details>
